claims.content: Language is the central medium of instructional communication and of subject learning processes; subject learning happens primarily through linguistic action.

claims.content: Educational language has central importance; its usage in subject teaching is based on everyday language but has particularities that can challenge students.

claims.content: Bildungssprache differs from everyday language through a stronger reference to written language and is therefore called conceptually written.
Typical features of Bildungssprache on word level include function-verb constructions, nominalized verbs and adjectives, and means to establish content coherence.
claims.cited_text: der Einsatz von Funktionsverbgefügen, nominalisierten Verben und Adjektiven

claims.content: A further language challenge lies in the technical language, comprising technical terms, subject-specific sentence structures, discourse functions and text types.

claims.content: Language requirements differ by subject, since each subject foregrounds different parts of educational language and has its own technical-language particularities.
